identification: Late Victorian (c1875-1895) mahogany hall stand / hall tree in Aesthetic-movement (Eastlake-influenced) taste: tall flat central pillar with incised trefoil/stop-fluted detail and pierced crest, ONE narrow arched bevel-less mirror slip set into the pillar, two tiers of large scrolled double arms with turned knob pegs (8 pegs), half-round serpentine console shelf (plain frieze, possibly a shallow drawer), two square supports and a central pierced scroll fretwork splat, brass wire umbrella rings at both sides, two original zinc/tin half-round drip pans on a shaped plinth base. About 197 cm. Possibly Australian-made in imported mahogany; looks honest, with polish wear on the shelf.
